text.p: Lehman Brothers has raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Comverse Technology Inc after it reported better-than-expected first-quarter results.

"Following another quarter of impressive results, we are raising our 1997 estimates from $1.42 to $1.50. Our fiscal 1998 estimates are increasing from $1.79 to $1.83," analyst Tim Luke wrote in the Lehman report.
The Israeli company posted first-quarter 1997 earnings per share (EPS) of $0.36 versus Lehman's estimate of $0.33. Comverse had $0.24 EPS in the first quarter of 1996.
Lehman said it was reiterating its 1-Buy rating for the stock based on a "buoyant" outlook for demand for enhanced services such as voice mail from wireless and wireline operators.
Comverse is a leading provider of special purpose computer telecommunication systems.
"We continue to believe our estimates are conservative and that they may be subject to upward revisions," Lehman said.
Lehman also raised its EPS estimates for the next three quarters of this year: second quarter to $0.37 from $0.35, third quarter to $0.38 from $0.36 and fourth quarter to $0.39 from $0.38.
It said Comverse's Trilogue voice messaging division continued to enjoy extremely robust demand, increasing 75 percent year-on-year to reach $43.6 million.
